description: The nodes of a mind map. One row per node. Import THIRTY-FIFTH (after mind_maps)
notes: ONE ROW PER NODE, not one JSON document per map. A map is edited from more than one device and a blob makes that last-write-wins - the same argument the checklist table makes, with more nodes to lose. Structural edits go through the batch endpoints so a 40-node map is still one request.
map_id and parent_id are TEXT holding row ids, not link_rows - consistent with project_id and board elsewhere, and a link field cannot express 'this is the root' (empty parent_id).
EXACTLY ONE node per map has an empty parent_id: the root. The client enforces it; nothing in Baserow can.

There are NO x/y columns, deliberately. Position is computed from the tree on every render. Storing positions would mean the layout can no longer tidy the map, which is most of what a mind map is for.
side only means anything for the root's children - it decides which way a top-level branch grows. Deeper nodes inherit their branch's side.
task_id points at a user_tasks row when this node IS a task. Deleting the node never deletes the task, and the confirm dialog says so.
sort_order positions a node among its siblings. The client renumbers on reorder; gaps are harmless.

user_id.description: Xano user id as a string. EVERY read filters on this

parent_id.description: mind_map_nodes row id. EMPTY means this is the root

side.description: Which way a top-level branch grows

task_id.description: user_tasks row id, when this node IS a task
